result.markdown: --- title: "Session 1 — Time-to-Event Data" subtitle: "Censoring · survival and hazard · the Surv object · person-time and rates · Lab 1" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Regression workshop: outcomes that are a **measurement** or a **yes/no** - Today: the outcome is **how long until something happens**: death, relapse, recovery, default from treatment - By the end you can: - say what **censoring** is, and why you cannot drop or average censored patients - define **survival**, **hazard** and **cumulative incidence** - build a `Surv` object and compute **person-time** and an **incidence rate** - describe **follow-up** correctly ::: ## Our data: a synthetic TB cohort ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} - **600 adults** starting TB treatment, followed for up to **24 months** - Outcome: **death**; `time_months` and `status` (1 = died, 0 = censored) - Predictors: age, sex, HIV, diabetes, smoking, BMI, **MDR-TB**, smear status, **DOT** (supervised treatment) - Invented, but built to behave like a real cohort ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tb |> select(id, age, hiv, mdr_tb, treatment, time_months, status) |> head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 7 id age hiv mdr_tb treatment time_months status 1 TB001 43 Negative No Self-administered 7.8 0 2 TB002 46 Negative No DOT 15.2 0 3 TB003 15 Negative No DOT 23.8 0 4 TB004 69 Negative No Self-administered 2.6 0 5 TB005 73 Negative No DOT 20.7 0 6 TB006 42 Negative No DOT 19.9 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} table(tb$status) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 0 1 487 113 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Topic 1 — Why survival analysis? {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Two problems with ordinary methods ::: {.incremental} - **Different follow-up:** a patient enrolled last month has had little time to die; one enrolled two years ago has had a lot. Comparing **proportions** who died ignores this - **Censoring:** for many patients we **do not observe** the event ::: ::: {.key} **Censored** = we know the patient was alive **at least until** their last contact, but not what happened afterwards. ::: | Why censored | Example | |---|---| | **Administrative** | still alive when the study ended | | **Lost to follow-up** | moved away, stopped attending | | **Competing event** | died of something else (a different question; see Session 5) | ## Censored patients still carry information ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} tb |> slice(1:15) |> mutate(row = row_number(), outcome = ifelse(status == 1, "Died", "Censored")) |> ggplot(aes(y = reorder(id, -row))) + geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = time_months, yend = reorder(id, -row)), colour = "grey60") + geom_point(aes(x = time_months, colour = outcome, shape = outcome), size = 3) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(Died = col_red, Censored = col_blue)) + labs(x = "Months of follow-up", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s1_time_to_event_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Each line is one patient; a **dot at the end** marks death or censoring - A censored patient contributes **their time at risk** up to the last contact - **Dropping** them wastes information and **biases** towards early deaths; **treating them as survivors forever** biases the other way ::: ## The three quantities | Quantity | Meaning | |---|---| | **Survival** S(t) | probability of being **alive beyond** time t | | **Hazard** h(t) | the **instantaneous rate** of dying at t, among those still alive | | **Cumulative incidence** | 1 − S(t): the probability of **having died by** t | ::: {.key} The **hazard** is a **rate** (events per person-time), not a probability. Cox regression (Session 4) models the hazard. ::: # Topic 2 — The Surv object {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Time and event together ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y <- Surv(tb$time_months, tb$status) head(y, 10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 7.8+ 15.2+ 23.8+ 2.6+ 20.7+ 19.9+ 3.8+ 19.4+ 14.9+ 17.7+ ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `Surv(time, event)` pairs each follow-up time with its event indicator - A **`+`** after a time marks a **censored** observation (still alive at least that long) - Check the coding: **1 = event**, 0 = censored (factor and TRUE/FALSE also work, but check!) - This object goes on the left of every survival model: `survfit(Surv(...) ~ group)`, `coxph(Surv(...) ~ x)` ::: ## Do not summarise survival times with a mean ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(mean_all = mean(tb$time_months), mean_among_deaths = mean(tb$time_months[tb$status == 1])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean_all mean_among_deaths 14.873500 5.780531 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.bad} Neither number is a survival time. The first mixes deaths and censored times; the second looks only at those who died and **ignores everyone who survived**, so it is biased downwards. ::: # Topic 3 — Person-time and rates {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Incidence rate ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} py <- sum(tb$time_months) / 12 c(deaths = sum(tb$status), person_years = round(py, 1), rate_per_100_py = round(sum(tb$status) / py * 100, 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` deaths person_years rate_per_100_py 113.0 743.7 15.2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Rate** = events / person-time at risk (here per 100 person-years) - It uses **everyone's** time, censored or not - Valid if the hazard is roughly **constant**; Kaplan-Meier (Session 2) removes that assumption ::: ## Describing follow-up honestly ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rkm <- survfit(Surv(time_months, 1 - status) ~ 1, data = tb) c(median_raw_time = median(tb$time_months), median_followup_reverse_KM = unname(summary(rkm)$table["median"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` median_raw_time median_followup_reverse_KM 16.7 18.1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The **reverse Kaplan-Meier** swaps the roles of event and censoring, so it asks "how long would a typical patient be followed *if they did not die*?". The **median of the raw times** is pulled down by deaths and understates follow-up. ::: ## Checklist before any analysis ::: {.good} 1. Define **time zero** (start of treatment, diagnosis) and the **event** precisely 2. Check **time** is positive and in one unit; **status** is coded 0/1 3. Count **events** and **censored**; tabulate **why** censored 4. Report **median follow-up** (reverse KM), person-time and events ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 1 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `survival-workshop/labs/lab1_data.R` - `table()` of status and censoring reasons - `Surv()`: the `+` marks censored times - person-years, a rate per 100 person-years, reverse Kaplan-Meier ::: **Time:** 30 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a380bk.h0q6ed" data-show="VGhlaXIgMTcgbW9udGhzIGF0IHJpc2ssIGFzIGEgY2Vuc29yZWQgb2JzZXJ2YXRpb24=" data-explain="QSBjZW5zb3JlZCBwYXRpZW50IGlzIGtub3duIHRvIGhhdmUgc3Vydml2ZWQgdG8gdGhlIGxh c3QgY29udGFjdC4gU3Vydml2YWwgbWV0aG9kcyB1c2UgdGhhdCB0aW1lIGF0IHJpc2ssIHRo ZW4gZHJvcCB0aGUgcGF0aWVudCBmcm9tIHRoZSByaXNrIHNldC4gRHJvcHBpbmcgb3IgYXNz dW1pbmcgc3Vydml2YWwgb3IgZGVhdGggYWxsIGJpYXMgdGhlIGVzdGltYXRlLg=="} What does a patient who was alive at the last clinic visit (month 17) and then moved away contribute to the analysis? - Nothing, since the outcome for this patient is unknown - A death at month 17, since no later contact exists - Their 17 months at risk, as a censored observation - An observation that must be treated as survival forever ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a38dk8.h0qkvp" data-show="UGF0aWVudHMgZGlmZmVyIGluIGZvbGxvdy11cCwgc28gYSBwcm9wb3J0aW9uIG1peGVzIHVu ZXF1YWwgdGltZSBhdCByaXNr" data-explain="UGF0aWVudHMgZW5yb2xsZWQgbGF0ZXIgd2VyZSBvYnNlcnZlZCBmb3IgbGVzcyB0aW1lLCBz byBmZXdlciBoYXZlIGhhZCB0aGUgY2hhbmNlIHRvIGRpZS4gUmF0ZXMgKGV2ZW50cyBwZXIg cGVyc29uLXRpbWUpIGFuZCBLYXBsYW4tTWVpZXIgZXN0aW1hdGVzIHVzZSBlYWNoIHBhdGll bnQncyB0aW1lIGF0IHJpc2su"} A TB cohort has 113 deaths among 600 patients. Why is 'mortality = 113/600 = 19%' a weak summary? - The number of deaths is too small to be divided by 600 patients, so it is unstable - Patients differ in follow-up, so a proportion mixes unequal time at risk - Mortality is reported as a count and should not be given as a percentage - The 19% ignores the fact that some of the patients in the cohort were female ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a38qsy.h0qzd3" data-show="VGhlIHBhdGllbnQgd2FzIGNlbnNvcmVkIGF0IDE3LjIgbW9udGhz" data-explain="VGhlIHBsdXMgc2lnbiBtYXJrcyBhIGNlbnNvcmVkIHRpbWU6IHRoZSBwYXRpZW50IHdhcyBz dGlsbCBldmVudC1mcmVlIGF0IDE3LjIgbW9udGhzLCBhbmQgaXMgbm90IG9ic2VydmVkIGFm dGVyd2FyZHMu"} In the output of a Surv object, 17.2+ means what? - The patient died at 17.2 months - The patient survived exactly 17.2 months in total - The patient was censored at 17.2 months - The patient had a second event after 17.2 months ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a3941o.h0rduh" data-show="VGhlIGluc3RhbnRhbmVvdXMgZXZlbnQgcmF0ZSBhbW9uZyB0aG9zZSBzdGlsbCBldmVudC1m cmVl" data-explain="VGhlIGhhemFyZCBpcyBhIHJhdGUsIGV2ZW50cyBwZXIgdW5pdCBvZiB0aW1lIGFtb25nIHRo b3NlIHN0aWxsIGF0IHJpc2suIFN1cnZpdmFsIGlzIGEgcHJvYmFiaWxpdHk7IHRoZSBtZWRp YW4gaXMgYSB0aW1lOyBkZWF0aHMgb3ZlciBwYXRpZW50cyBpcyBhIGNydWRlIHByb3BvcnRp b24u"} What is the hazard in survival analysis? - The probability of surviving beyond a given time point in the cohort - The total number of deaths divided by the total number of patients - The median time until the event occurs for half of the patients - The instantaneous event rate among those still event-free ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="a39haa.h0rsbr" data-show="RGVhdGhzIHNob3J0ZW4gcmF3IHRpbWVzLCBzbyB0aGVpciBtZWRpYW4gdW5kZXJzdGF0ZXMg Zm9sbG93LXVw" data-explain="UGF0aWVudHMgd2hvIGRpZWQgc3RvcCBiZWluZyBmb2xsb3dlZCwgd2hpY2ggcHVsbHMgcmF3 IHRpbWVzIGRvd24uIFRyZWF0aW5nIGNlbnNvcmluZyBhcyB0aGUgZXZlbnQgc2hvd3MgaG93 IGxvbmcgYSBwYXRpZW50IHdvdWxkIGJlIGZvbGxvd2VkIGlmIHRoZXkgZGlkIG5vdCBkaWUu "} Why is the reverse Kaplan-Meier median a better description of follow-up than the median of the raw follow-up times? - Deaths shorten raw times, so their median understates follow-up - The reverse method removes all of the patients who were censored - Raw follow-up times cannot be calculated when some patients died - The reverse method gives the median survival time of the patients ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Censoring**: observed up to a time, then unknown; keep these patients - Survival S(t), hazard h(t), cumulative incidence 1 − S(t) - `Surv(time, event)`: a **+** means censored - Use **person-time rates**, not a mean of follow-up times; report **median follow-up** by reverse KM ::: **Next:** Session 2: Kaplan-Meier curves

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
